brief.title: Business card: Crumb & Co. Bakery
brief.brief:
Design a two-sided US business card (3.5 x 2 in) for Crumb & Co. Bakery. It is open Tuesday to Sunday, 7am to 3pm, and takes preorders at crumbandco.example. Those are the only facts: do not add reviews, ratings, awards, a phone number, an address or anything else.

Deliver both sides as one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS and inline SVG only). On screen, show the front and the back as cards that scale fluidly to fit a phone and a desktop without sideways scrolling; you may add a short screen-only note beside the cards (not on them) stating the trim size and how to print. For print, add an @media print block with @page { size: 3.5in 2in; margin: 0 } so it prints as exactly two pages, page 1 the front and page 2 the back, each filling its page, with any screen-only notes hidden.

requirements.description: Shows the bakery name "Crumb & Co. Bakery" on the card.
States the hours: Tuesday to Sunday (Tue-Sun), 7am to 3pm.
Contains no invented reviews, ratings, awards or other facts beyond the brief, and presents a front and a back side.

artifacts.title: Crumb & Co. Bakery | Business Card (Front and Back)

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The page meets all four requirements: the name, hours, preorder line and two-sided layout are present, and no invented facts appear.

checks.reason: The back shows "Crumb & Co. Bakery" as a heading, and the front shows "Crumb & Co. Bakery" split across two lines in the large wordmark.
The back lists "Open: Tuesday to Sunday" and "Hours: 7am to 3pm" in the hours table, visible in both the desktop and phone screenshots.
The back reads "Preorders at crumbandco.example", with the URL in accent italic.
The page contains only the brief's facts: name, days, hours, preorder URL. It has no reviews, ratings, awards, phone or address, and it presents separate front and back cards.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean, restrained two-sided card that carries every fact in the brief without embellishment. The serif wordmark on the front and the ruled hours table on the back read clearly at both desktop and 390px phone widths.
strengths: Front wordmark is large and well-spaced, with the accent-coloured ampersand giving a clear focal point.
Back uses a ruled Open and Hours table, so the two schedule facts are easy to scan.
The page fits 390px with no sideways overflow, and the card text stays legible on the phone.
weaknesses: The front shows only "Tuesday to Sunday" with no hours, so a reader of the front alone gets no times.
The back's top band holds only the name, leaving a fairly sparse upper area on the card.
Small uppercase labels such as OPEN and HOURS are light grey-brown on cream and may be faint in print.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a quiet, traditional bakery card that sticks strictly to the supplied facts.

artifacts.title: Crumb & Co. Bakery | Business Card (3.5 x 2 in, front and back)

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The page meets all four requirements: the name, hours, preorder line and both card sides are present, with no invented facts.

checks.reason: The front card shows the name "Crumb & Co. Bakery" as its h1 heading, rendered large and centred in both the desktop and phone screenshots.
The back card states "Tuesday to Sunday (Tue-Sun)" and "7am to 3pm" in the hours block, shown on three lines in the screenshots.
The back card includes the pill-shaped line "Preorders at crumbandco.example", visible in both screenshots, though it wraps onto two lines.
The page adds no reviews, ratings, awards, phone number or address. The only extra text is the "Open" label, which restates the brief, and the page presents a front card and a back card.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean two-sided card that uses only the supplied facts: the front carries the bakery name and loaf illustration, and the back carries the hours and preorder line. It reads clearly at both desktop and phone widths.
strengths: The front shows the bakery name large and centred over a loaf illustration, with a berry rule beneath it.
The back puts the hours and preorder pill in a clear hierarchy, with "Open" as a small label above.
Phone layout fits the 390px width with no overflow, and each card keeps its proportions.
weaknesses: The back card's hours wrap to three lines ("(Tue-Sun)" drops onto its own line), which makes the block taller than it needs to be.
The decorative corner circles are cropped at the card edges and sit close to the text on the back, which looks slightly busy at small size.
The preorder line wraps onto two lines inside its pill, so it reads less cleanly than a single line would.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a simple, brief-faithful card with no extra claims to verify or remove.

artifacts.title: Crumb & Co. Bakery | Business Card (3.5 x 2 in)

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The page meets all four requirements: the name, hours, preorder line and two-sided card are present, with no invented facts.

checks.reason: The front card shows "CRUMB & CO." in large black type with "BAKERY" beneath it, so the bakery name appears on the card.
The back card shows "HOURS / TUESDAY TO SUNDAY / 7am to 3pm (Tue-Sun)", and the front tagline repeats "Tuesday to Sunday · 7am to 3pm".
The back card's honey-coloured block reads "Preorders at crumbandco.example" under an "Order ahead" label.

The card text contains only the brief's facts: name, hours and preorder URL, with no reviews, ratings, awards, phone or address. Front and back sections are both present, and the print notes sit outside the cards.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean, bold two-sided card that carries exactly the brief's facts: the orange front with the name and hours tagline, and the dark back with hours and a honey-yellow preorder block. The layout reads well at both widths.
strengths: Back card has a clear hierarchy: small honey label, large "TUESDAY TO SUNDAY", then "7am to 3pm (Tue-Sun)".
The preorder URL sits in a high-contrast honey block, so it stands out on the dark back.
No invented reviews, awards, phone or address; only the brief's facts appear on the cards.
weaknesses: On the 390px phone view, the "BAKERY" line sits on the edge of the dark bottom band on the front, so it looks cramped.
The front card has little beyond the name and a small tagline, so it looks sparse next to the dense back.
The screen view adds a print-notes panel beside the cards; it is hidden in print as required but takes space on desktop.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a bold, minimal print card that shows only the hours and the preorder address.
